extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and general readers interested in American literature, democratic art, and oratory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative principles for judging poetry, literary art, and public oratory in the context of 19th-century American democratic culture; includes guidance on artistic purpose, maturity, audience, and spiritual sincerity. Useful for poets, critics, and scholars assessing literary value and rhetorical effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual judgment (age, politics, aim, times)
rubrics_metrics.description: No great poem or other literary or artistic work of any scope can be essentially consider'd without weighing first the age, politics (or want of politics) and aim, visible forms, unseen soul, and current times, out of the midst of which it rises and is formulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a work, explicitly account for its historical moment, political background, authorial aim, and the cultural 'soil' that produced it. Compare to exemplars of its period (e.g., Biblical canticles, Homer, Dante, Shakespeare) to understand functions and departures. Avoid judging a work solely by anachronistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic art emerges from democratic development
rubrics_metrics.description: Democratic art results of democratic development, from tinge, true nationality, belief, in the one setting up from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a national or democratic literature grows organically from the people's conditions and convictions. Look for autochthonic, interior, local evolutions in style and subject matter rather than mere imitation of aristocratic or foreign forms. Expect a slow, constitutional emergence rather than instant formal invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose over polished form
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson of Nature undoubtedly is, to proceed with single purpose toward the result necessitated, and for which the time has arrived, utterly regardless of the outputs of shape, appearance or criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the work's central purpose and expressive truth rather than surface polish, ornate conceits, or fashionable forms. Treat style and form as instruments that must not usurp or obscure the work's intent; acceptable for form to be unpolished if it serves purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid domination of art by style/concetti
rubrics_metrics.description: I have not only not bother'd much about style, form, art, etc., but confess to more or less apathy ... asking nothing of them but negative advantages--that they should never impede me, and never under any circumstances, or for their own purposes only, assume any mastery over me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: excessive devotion to fine rhyme, spicy verbalism, jewelry, concetti, or surface elegance. Critique works that sacrifice substance to stylistic effects. Encourage restraint where ornamentation distracts from moral or democratic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral/spiritual/heroic personal illustration as highest poetic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the production (and on the most copious scale) of loftiest moral, spiritual and heroic personal illustrations--a great native Literature headed with a Poetry stronger and sweeter than any yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that present strong moral, spiritual, or heroic exemplars in living form. Evaluate poetry by its capacity to incarnate ideals and to produce exemplars that uplift the national character; deprioritize purely decorative or solely entertaining verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience appetite matters: need great readers
rubrics_metrics.description: To have great heroic poetry we need great readers--a heroic appetite and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the existence and reception of ambitious poetry depends on an audience able and willing to receive it. When assessing the potential impact of a work, consider contemporary readership sophistication, appetite, and civic-cultural conditions that cultivate 'great readers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature, accreted voice (value of great old age)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final proof of song or personality is a sort of matured, accreted, superb, evoluted, almost divine, impalpable diffuseness and atmosphere or invisible magnetism ... Completed fruitage like this comes (in my opinion) to a grand age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give special weight to works or voices that show long maturation—an accumulated atmosphere, subtlety, and integrated wisdom. See advanced age and continuity of production as sources of depth rather than as weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's universality and inclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is one, is not partial, but includes all times and forms and sorts--is not exclusively aristocratic or democratic, or oriental or occidental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art with an eye to its capacity to encompass diverse modes and traditions. Avoid rigid categorization (aristocratic vs democratic) and value cross-pollination and universality in form and spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical efficacy relies on unnameable personal magnetism
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is ... an unnameable something behind oratory ... that unnameable constitutional something Elias Hicks emanated from his very heart to the hearts of his audience ... a sympathetic germ, probably rapport, lurking in every human eligibility ... launch'd out only by powerful human magnetism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging oratory, account for intangible qualities—personal sincerity, rapport, charisma, and 'magnetism'—that transcend technical skill. Examples include speakers who move audiences despite lack of polished rhetoric. Anti-pattern: evaluating oratory solely on rhetorical devices and ignoring presence and affective connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the inner light and moral-mystical conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: One of his old never-remitted appeals ... to that moral mystical portion of human nature, the inner light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess religious or moral speech by its ability to awaken the listener's inner conscience and aspiration toward the ideal, rather than by doctrinal correctness or ritual observance. Effective preaching addresses latent remorse for worldly life and cultivates inward transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious authenticity judged by inward life and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Christian religion ... consists neither in rites or Bibles or sermons or Sundays--but in noiseless secret ecstasy and unremitted aspiration, in purity, in a good practical life, in charity to the poor and toleration to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate religious authorship, testimony, or characters by the sincerity and practicality of their moral life (charity, purity, toleration) rather than by formal adherence to rites, offices, or creeds. Anti-pattern: equating religious value with outward observance or institutional trappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary typology as critical shorthand (style/persona descriptors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterizations of poets: Longfellow 'reminiscent, polish'd, elegant'; Whittier 'stands for morality...lean and ascetic'; Bryant 'meditative, serious...lyrical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use typological descriptions to situate poets within aesthetic and moral traditions; these descriptors help signal reader expectations and comparative evaluation. But avoid reducing a poet to a single type or dismissing works that depart from their nominal category.
